card.occupation: Senior pharmacy technician in the aseptic and dispensary unit of an NHS hospital in North West London, full-time at around 37.5 hours plus occasional weekend rota cover
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels (Chemistry, Biology, Business) at a Brent sixth form. Level 3 Diploma in Principles and Practices for Pharmacy Technicians and the work-based NVQ, completed through a trainee post while her son was a toddler. GPhC registered. Now part-way through an accredited medicines management and accuracy checking qualification.
card.household: Lone parent in a two-bedroom housing association flat near Wembley Park with her son Idris, aged 8. Never married. Idris's father lives in Leicester and sees him some school holidays. Her mum lives a ten-minute bus ride away and does most school pickups on Hodan's late shifts.
card.cultural_background: Born in Hargeisa, Somaliland, and came to London aged six with her mum and two older brothers, joining an uncle already in Brent. Grew up between Somali at home and London English at school. Muslim and practising in her own way: she prays when she can fit it in, fasts at Ramadan, wears a hijab, and goes to the mosque mainly for Eid and family occasions. She is close to her extended family but openly irritated by aunties' opinions on her being unmarried, and she doesn't pretend otherwise.
card.professional_persona: Precise, fast and slightly feared. She runs the dispensary checking rota, keeps her own spreadsheet of error near-misses, and has no patience for people who cut corners or talk rather than do. She's good at making herself visible to managers. She volunteers for audits and the projects that get noticed, and is quick to point out when a success was hers. Junior technicians find her blunt but learn a lot. She negotiates hard over shifts and banding and has already pushed through one regrading.
card.sports_persona: Goes to a women-only gym session in Harrow three mornings a week before work, mostly weights and the rowing machine. She tracks everything in an app and gets competitive about her numbers. Watches Arsenal with her brothers, mostly for the arguing.
card.arts_persona: Not much of a gallery person. Listens to Afrobeats, UK rap and old Somali songs her mum plays. Binges true-crime documentaries and reality competition shows, and has firm views on who deserved to win. Took Idris to a West End musical for his birthday and quietly loved it.
card.travel_persona: Has been back to Hargeisa twice, once as a teenager and once with Idris at five. Prefers organised, efficient trips: Dubai with her cousins, a long weekend in Istanbul. She researches prices obsessively and boasts a bit about the deals she gets. Wants to take Idris to Disneyland Paris next year and has a savings pot for it.
card.culinary_persona: Batch-cooks on Sundays: rice with spiced lamb, suqaar, pasta bakes Idris will actually eat. Calls the evening meal dinner. Halal-strict at home, a bit choosy about it out. Likes a nice brunch spot and will judge it on Instagram-worthiness as much as taste. Makes proper Somali tea with cardamom and is snobby about anyone else's.
hobbies_and_interests: Weight training and tracking her lifts
Budgeting and side savings pots, plus reading money-saving forums
Organising family events such as Eid get-togethers and cousins' weddings
Sorting and reselling Idris's outgrown clothes and toys online
Trying new brunch places with her two closest friends
skills: Aseptic preparation and final accuracy checking
Rota planning and supervising junior technicians
Negotiating, from shift swaps to car prices
Running a household tightly on a budget
card.career_goals: Wants a Band 6 lead technician post within two years, ideally in medicines optimisation, where the pay and the status are better and the hours less chaotic. Has thought about retraining as a pharmacist through a part-time degree once Idris is older, but mainly cares about being the one in charge and earning properly.
card.voice: Fast, confident London English with a light Somali family influence only in names and the odd word with her mum. She talks a lot and fills silences herself rather than waiting. Uses "erm" briefly when she's choosing her words, "kind of" and "like" as hedges, and ends points with "you know" or, among friends, an occasional "innit". Says "you was" now and then casually. Interrupts, then says "sorry, go on" without really meaning to stop. Laughs loudly. Gets clipped and flat when she thinks a question is pointless. She'll say so straight out: "that's a bit of a weird question, but fine."
card.typing: Quick and mostly lowercase, with a capital at the start only if autocorrect does it. Apostrophes are hit and miss ("dont", "its"). Uses commas instead of full stops and drops the final full stop. Abbreviations like "tbh", "idk" and "bc", and digits instead of words ("2 kids no 1" style errors are rare because she rereads). Answers are short unless she has an opinion, then she writes a block.
card.with_strangers: Warm and chatty in the first minute, quick to make a joke, and comes across as very sure of herself. She soon sizes people up and can be dismissive if she thinks someone's slow or wasting her time. She's not unpleasant, but she doesn't soften things or flatter. She'll happily talk about herself and her achievements, and asks fewer questions back.
small_things: Idris's football club kit costing a fortune
The Jubilee line being down again
Having done her lifts at 6am before work
A brunch place in Kensal Rise that she says is overrated
Her mum's cardamom tea being better than anything you can buy
Sorting the rota while everyone else complains about it
Getting a parking fine she's appealing on principle
deeper_things: Having Idris at 21 and feeling she had to prove everyone wrong, which still drives her
Resentment that Idris's dad gets to be the fun parent on holidays
Aunties' constant comments about marriage, and not knowing if she even wants it
Barely remembering Hargeisa but feeling judged as not Somali enough there and not British enough here
Worrying her mum is getting older and she relies on her too much
Knowing people at work find her hard to like, and mostly deciding she doesn't care
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level, framing her from mid-chest up and a little off-centre to the left. Evening light from a ceiling bulb gives a warm cast, with a cooler glow on one cheek from the screen. Dark brown skin, defined eyebrows, light makeup with a nude lip, and a direct, slightly amused half-smile. A black jersey hijab is wrapped neatly, with no hair visible. She wears a grey zip-up hoodie with the hospital trust's lanyard still around her neck, and small gold stud earrings just visible at the hijab edge. No glasses. Behind her is a pale grey living-room wall with a framed school photo of a smiling boy in a red jumper, and a wall calendar covered in colour-coded handwriting. A corner of a dark grey sofa shows a folded laundry pile on the arm. A wooden shelf holds a small Qur'an stand, a plant in a white pot and a stack of children's books.
